correctness.rationale: The complex is the downward closure of surviving perfect matchings, not the ordinary matching complex. Independent code reenumerated 36 original perfect matchings, 120 automorphisms and all 435 distinct unordered double faults in eight orbits. The full Hasse graphs verified acyclicity; removing the empty-face pairing leaves one critical basepoint. The critical 2-/3-cell profiles in the listed orbit order are (0,0),(2,2),(1,1),(1,0),(1,0),(1,1),(1,1),(1,2). The signed degree matrix vanishes except for a single primitive nonzero column (1,−1) at (0,5). The CW two-skeleton is a wedge of 2-spheres, so Hurewicz identifies the entire attaching-map data with these degree matrices. Integral basis changes on source and target wedges leave the homotopy cofiber unchanged and cancel the unit entry. This proves the counts 60,120,240,15 for the four types and the disappearance of torsion. Intact and one-fault torsion are credited antecedent results, not new consequences of the census.
residual_risks: The separate replay implements the same Morse pairing strategy; the direct mod-2 and mod-3 homology ranks corroborate it but do not prove integral torsion-freeness by themselves. No conclusion about inclusion-induced homomorphisms follows from the census.

evidence: GP(10,2) is the dodecahedral graph. Independence complexes studied by Kim have a different face predicate; even ordinary matchings would require a nontrivial extendability restriction. value.rationale: This is a natural fault threshold for a known torsion-bearing, symmetric extension complex. The complete homotopy-type census answers both sharp robustness (one fault is insufficient and every two distinct faults suffice) and what replaces the torsion, including the effect of incidence and disjoint-pair orbits. The invariant is not determined by a matching count or a homology calculation over one field.
residual_risks: It does not establish a fullerene family principle or classify greater fault counts; its value is the motivated complete classification for the canonical graph.
